package PKG

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"testing"

	"fakemod/rt"
)

var le = binary.LittleEndian

// bld builds a body the way 4.5 describes it, independently of the generated code under test.
type bld struct{ b []byte }

func (w *bld) align(n int) *bld {
	for len(w.b)%n != 0 {
		w.b = append(w.b, 0)
	}
	return w
}

func (w *bld) raw(p ...byte) *bld { w.b = append(w.b, p...); return w }

func (w *bld) u16(v uint16) *bld { w.align(2); w.b = le.AppendUint16(w.b, v); return w }
func (w *bld) u32(v uint32) *bld { w.align(4); w.b = le.AppendUint32(w.b, v); return w }
func (w *bld) u64(v uint64) *bld { w.align(8); w.b = le.AppendUint64(w.b, v); return w }

func (w *bld) str(s string) *bld {
	w.u32(uint32(len(s)))
	w.b = append(w.b, s...)
	w.b = append(w.b, 0)
	return w
}

func (w *bld) bytes(p []byte) *bld {
	w.u32(uint32(len(p)))
	w.b = append(w.b, p...)
	return w
}

func (w *bld) body() []byte { return w.b }

// srv answers the next request of a test.
type srv struct {
	t    *testing.T
	next func(req []byte) []byte
	cl   *Client
}

func newSrv(t *testing.T) *srv {
	s := &srv{t: t}
	s.cl = &Client{c: rt.NewConn(hqqIface, func(req []byte) []byte {
		if s.next == nil {
			t.Fatalf("unexpected request %x", req)
		}
		next := s.next
		s.next = nil
		return next(req)
	})}
	return s
}

func respFrame(req []byte, flags uint8, status uint32, body []byte) []byte {
	f := make([]byte, 16+len(body))
	f[0], f[1] = 2, flags
	copy(f[2:4], req[2:4])
	copy(f[4:8], req[4:8])
	le.PutUint32(f[8:], uint32(len(body)))
	le.PutUint32(f[12:], status)
	copy(f[16:], body)
	return f
}

const (
	fDetail = 1
	fFail   = 2
)

// expect checks the next request (opcode and body) and answers it with a response frame.
func (s *srv) expect(op uint16, wantBody []byte, flags uint8, resp []byte) {
	s.t.Helper()
	s.next = func(req []byte) []byte {
		s.t.Helper()
		if got := le.Uint16(req[2:]); got != op {
			s.t.Errorf("request op %d, want %d", got, op)
		}
		if got := req[16:]; !bytes.Equal(got, wantBody) {
			s.t.Errorf("request body\n got %x\nwant %x", got, wantBody)
		}
		if got := le.Uint32(req[8:]); int(got) != len(wantBody) {
			s.t.Errorf("request total %d, want %d", got, len(wantBody))
		}
		return respFrame(req, flags, 0, resp)
	}
}

// status answers the next request with a call-level status.
func (s *srv) status(status uint32, msg string) {
	s.next = func(req []byte) []byte { return respFrame(req, 0, status, new(bld).str(msg).body()) }
}

// reply answers the next request without checking it.
func (s *srv) reply(flags uint8, resp []byte) {
	s.next = func(req []byte) []byte { return respFrame(req, flags, 0, resp) }
}

func (s *srv) conn() *rt.Conn { return s.cl.Conn() }

func (s *srv) requests() int { return len(s.conn().Requests) }

// wantMalformed fails unless err is the protocol error of a malformed response, and checks that the
// next call is still possible (the decoder was released).
func wantMalformed(t *testing.T, what string, err error) {
	t.Helper()
	var pe *rt.ProtocolError
	if !asErr(err, &pe) {
		t.Errorf("%s: error %v, want a malformed response", what, err)
	}
}

func asErr[T error](err error, target *T) bool {
	for err != nil {
		if e, ok := err.(T); ok {
			*target = e
			return true
		}
		u, ok := err.(interface{ Unwrap() error })
		if !ok {
			return false
		}
		err = u.Unwrap()
	}
	return false
}

func hexs(b []byte) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%x", b) }
